claim: For Algorithm 1 of Lu--Wang on the admissible scalar problem \(g(z)=a z^2/2\), \(q=\delta_{[-R,R]}\), and \(c(z)=z^2-R_c^2\) with \(a>0\), \(R_c>R\), nonzero \(z^0\), and a radius large enough that every reached line-search trial remains in the box, the surrogate constraint is inactive and every inner trial has \(z^{k+1,i}=(1-a/L_i)z^k\), where \(L_i=\underline L\rho^i\). A nonzero trial is accepted exactly when \(2L_i\ge a+\beta\), so every nonterminal outer iteration accepts at the same index \(i_*=\lceil\log_\rho((a+\beta)/(2\underline L))\rceil_+\) and at \(L_*=\underline L\rho^{i_*}\). With the exact smoothness constant \(L=a\), this \(i_*\) is exactly the upper bound in the source's Theorem 4, so that per-outer bound is attained at every outer iteration. The accepted recurrence is \(z^{k+1}=q_*z^k\), where \(q_*=1-a/L_*\) and \(|q_*|<1\). If \(L_*=a\), the method reaches zero and satisfies its stopping test on the first accepted outer step. If \(L_*\ne a\), the stopping test is exactly \(C_*|z^k|\le\tau\), where \(C_*=a|a-L_*|/L_*\), and the first stopping outer index is \(K_*=\lceil\log(C_*|z^0|/\tau)/\log(1/|q_*|)\rceil_+\). Consequently the method solves exactly \((K_*+1)(i_*+1)\) proximal subproblems, including \((K_*+1)i_*\) rejected trials. When \(i_*>0\), resetting the line search to \(\underline L\) therefore replays the same rejected curvature trials at every outer iteration; on this scalar family, starting each later outer iteration at the previously accepted \(L_*\) would save exactly \(K_*i_*\) rejected solves without changing the accepted step.
integrity: The proof is symbolic; the included finite computation checks one representative parameter choice only. Earliest-public-date and primary-classification ownership are taken from the first public arXiv record. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: Exact for the stated scalar quadratic with a strictly inactive constraint and a box large enough to contain all reached trials. The warm-start comparison is a family-specific counterfactual, not a general convergence theorem.
title: Exact repeated-reset backtracking cost in fixed-baseline SCP
